M-ACCESS.title: Authentication, access control and physical security

KIA-A2.title: Risk matrix: assessing and ranking risks
KIA-A2.description:
Each risk has a likelihood (1–5) and an impact (1–5). Risk level = likelihood × impact. Determine the category using the 5×5 teaching scale below and print the risks in decreasing order of level (on a tie — in input order).

  • 1–4: Past (low)
  • 5–9: O'rta (medium)
  • 10–16: Yuqori (high)
  • 17–25: Kritik (critical)

Print the category words exactly as shown in code. The scale is chosen for a teaching example; organizations set their own thresholds in their risk policy.
KIA-A2.instructions: Input: n; n lines with name likelihood impact (the name has no spaces). Output: on each line name level category.

KIA-A5C.title: Caesar cipher
KIA-A5C.description: In the Caesar cipher every Latin letter is shifted k positions in the alphabet (A follows Z). Letter case is preserved, other characters do not change. A negative k means decryption.
KIA-A5C.instructions: Input: line 1 k; line 2 the text. Output: the encrypted text.
KIA-A5C.constraintsText: −1000 ≤ k ≤ 1000; the text consists of ASCII characters only.

KIA-A5V.title: Vigenère cipher
KIA-A5V.description: The Vigenère cipher is a polyalphabetic substitution: each letter of the text is shifted by the value of the next key letter (A = 0, B = 1, …). The key index advances only on letters; spaces and punctuation do not change.
KIA-A5V.instructions: Input: line 1 E (encrypt) or D (decrypt); line 2 the key (letters only); line 3 the text. Output: the result.
KIA-A5V.constraintsText: Key length 1–50; the text is ASCII.

KIA-A7.title: RSA: key generation, encryption and decryption
KIA-A7.description:
Small primes p and q and the public exponent e are given. Carry out the RSA steps:

  1. n = p·q, φ(n) = (p − 1)(q − 1);
  2. the private exponent d = e⁻¹ mod φ(n) (the extended Euclidean algorithm);
  3. the ciphertext c = mᵉ mod n;
  4. check: c^d mod n = m.

In real RSA p and q have hundreds of digits and padding (for example OAEP) is applied; here only the mathematical idea is studied.
KIA-A7.instructions: Input: p q e m. Output: on one line n φ d c decrypted_m.
KIA-A7.constraintsText: p, q < 10^6 prime; gcd(e, φ) = 1; 0 ≤ m < n.

KIA-A8.title: Checking integrity with SHA-256
KIA-A8.description: A hash function produces a fixed-length “fingerprint” from data of any length. Even if one character changes, the SHA-256 value becomes completely different (the avalanche effect). Compute the SHA-256 of a message and compare it with the given value.
KIA-A8.instructions: Input: line 1 the message (UTF-8); line 2 the expected hash (hex). Output: line 1 the computed hash (lowercase hex); line 2 Yaxlit (intact) or Buzilgan (corrupted) — print these words exactly.

KIA-A10.title: Password policy: rating password strength
KIA-A10.description:
Write a program that checks a password policy. 1 point for each criterion: length ≥ 8; length ≥ 12; a lowercase letter; an uppercase letter; a digit; a special character (a character that is neither a letter nor a digit). If the password is on the list of common passwords (password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, admin, parol, case-insensitive) — the score is 0.

  • 0–2: Zaif (weak)
  • 3–4: O'rtacha (medium)
  • 5–6: Kuchli (strong)

Print the level words exactly as shown in code.
KIA-A10.instructions: Input: n; n passwords (each on its own line, without spaces). Output: the score and level for each password.

KIA-A11.title: Linux permissions: from rwx to octal
KIA-A11.description: The ls -l command shows file permissions like -rwxr-xr--: the first character is the file type, then three characters each for the owner, the group and others. Each triple becomes an octal digit: r = 4, w = 2, x = 1. For example, rwxr-xr-- → 754 (chmod 754 file).
KIA-A11.instructions: Input: n; n lines with a 10-character permission string. Output: for each, the octal code and the file type — fayl (file), katalog (directory) or havola (link); print these words exactly.

KIA-Q-A1.title: Information security concepts
KIA-Q-A1.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: Which property of the CIA triad means that data is open only to authorized persons?
The amount in a bank account was changed without authorization. Which property was violated?
Against which property is a DoS attack primarily directed?
An unpatched program in a system is…
questions.explanation: A vulnerability is a weakness a threat can exploit. Risk is the combination of the likelihood and the consequences of a threat exploiting a vulnerability.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are controls (protective measures)?

KIA-Q-A3.title: Cybercrime and legal foundations
KIA-Q-A3.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: An employee of an organization abuses their authority to steal data. What type of threat is this?
In digital forensics, what is usually used to show that evidence has not changed?

options.text: Recording the hash value of the evidence copy

questions.prompt: The chain of custody documents by whom and when the evidence was handled.
What is sending an email meant to trick a victim into giving away a password called?
Cyberethics studies only actions prohibited by law.
questions.explanation: Ethics is broader than law: it also considers actions that are legal but morally wrong.

KIA-Q-A4.title: Security policy
KIA-Q-A4.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: Which document is at the highest, most general level of the hierarchy of security documents?
“An employee is given only the rights needed to do their job” — which principle is this?
What does a password policy usually include?

options.text: A procedure for telling the password to a colleague

questions.prompt: An acceptable use policy (AUP) defines how employees may use the organization's resources.

KIA-Q-A6.title: Symmetric encryption and AES
KIA-Q-A6.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: What is the main feature of symmetric encryption?

options.text: The same key is used for encryption and decryption
No key is used at all

questions.prompt: What is the AES block length in bits?
questions.explanation: The AES block length is always 128 bits; the key length can be 128, 192 or 256 bits.

questions.prompt: Which key lengths does AES support?
What type of cipher is the A5/1 algorithm?
In ECB mode identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks, so it is not recommended.

KIA-Q-A9.title: SSL/TLS and certificates
KIA-Q-A9.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: The browser checks who signed a site's certificate. Who is that?
Which TCP port does HTTPS use by default?
What information does an X.509 certificate contain?
questions.explanation: The private key is never included in a certificate — only its owner keeps it.

questions.prompt: A browser considers an expired certificate trustworthy.

KIA-Q-A12.title: Physical security
KIA-Q-A12.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: Which of these are physical security controls?
What is it called when an unauthorized person follows an employee through a door?
What is the most reliable way to destroy confidential data on an old hard disk?

options.text: Moving the files to the recycle bin
Physically destroying the disk or special overwriting
Installing the disk in another computer

questions.prompt: Fire and flood are man-made (human-caused) threats.

KIA-Q-A13.title: Monitoring network traffic
KIA-Q-A13.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: Which display filter shows only HTTP traffic in Wireshark?
What is switching a network card into a mode that accepts all frames called?
Why can a password sent over HTTP be seen in a sniffer?

options.text: The password is sent via DNS

questions.prompt: Network traffic should be analyzed only on an authorized network, your own, or a training network.

KIA-Q-A14.title: VPN
KIA-Q-A14.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a VPN?

options.text: Creating an encrypted tunnel over an open network

questions.prompt: Which of these are VPN protocols?
When a VPN is connected, the user is fully protected from malicious sites.
questions.explanation: A VPN encrypts traffic but does not protect against malware or phishing sites.

questions.prompt: At which OSI layer does IPSec work?

KIA-Q-A15.title: IoT security
KIA-Q-A15.instructions: Read each question carefully. In multiple-answer questions, select all correct options.

questions.prompt: One of the most common weaknesses of IoT devices?
Which malware organized large DDoS attacks in 2016 with a botnet of IoT devices?
Measures for protecting an IoT device:

options.text: Placing the device in a separate network segment
Opening all ports to the Internet

questions.prompt: In a cloud service, only the provider is responsible for data security.
questions.explanation: The shared responsibility model: the provider protects the infrastructure, while the customer protects their own data, access rights and settings.
